description: Revising old code: an existing std-only Rust tool, froid (a community pantry's cold-chain tool reading its fridge and freezer loggers' exports: check, latest, and digest, with a parser, a table module, command-line tests, docs, sample data, and four commits of history), whose digest command checks the files and then runs tools/digest.py, the pantry's older Python script, through python3 (found through CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR) and passes its output through: the state a careless earlier change left it in. The request says froid must run on a locked-down kiosk whose image holds nothing but the pantry's own binaries, where digest fails because it cannot run python3, and that the digest must print exactly what it prints today; it names neither the cause nor a technique. Removing the defect means froid computing and laying out the digest itself (the script reads the files again, groups readings by unit in first-seen order and by day, rounds means and medians with Python's round, picks the first of equally bad readings, and pads columns by characters). Keeping the script wherever python3 exists, or behind a setting, with a port elsewhere meets the ticket on the kiosk and keeps the defect (two implementations of one digest that must stay byte-identical, and every machine with python3 running code the kiosk never runs), so the checks hold the revision to being done right. Required: the build; digest on hidden exports byte for byte as the fixture's own froid prints it, in the ordinary root (host interpreters on PATH, working directory at the repository copy, froid at target/release/froid), in the sealed minimal root (only the binary and the C runtime, read-only, memfd_create and execveat refused, so a port to Node or Perl, an embedded copy of the script, or a carried interpreter fails), and in the recorded root with no interpreter started (every interpreter and shell on PATH, and anything named python, replaced by a recorder, so keeping the script for hosts that have python3 and a port only for hosts that do not fails); the shipped Rust (the .rs files cargo's dep-info names for froid, #[cfg(test)] and #[test] items left out) starting no interpreter or shell by literal name and naming neither tools/digest.py nor the host's Python library or its C API, so the script kept behind an opt-in variable, which no root can turn on, or Python run inside froid through libpython, which starts nothing, fails; check and latest unchanged on hidden files and the fixture's command-line tests restored and passing. Keeping or removing tools/digest.py is not judged, and a test that runs it as a parity oracle fails nothing. Measures: needs_interpreter, interpreters started, the rest of the static report on shipped Rust (see _shared/no_interpreter.py and _shared/no_spawn.py), the script's state, the README, the agent's own tests, commits. Agent arms need the Rust toolchain readable inside confinement, for example "readable": ["~/.rustup/toolchains/stable-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu", "~/.rustup/toolchains/stable-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin"] (the directory `rustc --print sysroot` names, and its bin); the check needs bubblewrap, the host's Rust toolchain (TRIAL_RUST_SYSROOT overrides it), and python3. The fixture's manifest is stored as Cargo.toml.in and renamed by setup.sh, for this repository's CI.
prompt: froid has to run on the new kiosk box in the back office from the November release on. It's a locked-down image with nothing on it but our own binaries, and `froid digest` fails there ("cannot run python3"). Could you get the digest working on the kiosk? Hélène's morning report and the board's spreadsheet both read the digest, so it has to print exactly what it prints today.

judge.question: The user asked for froid, a Rust command-line tool whose `digest` ran a Python script (tools/digest.py) through python3, to work on a kiosk whose image holds nothing but the pantry's own binaries (digest could not run python3 there), printing exactly what it prints today. Does the delivered froid compute and lay out the digest in its own Rust code, rather than running that script, a copy of it, a port of it to another language, or an interpreter it carries, on any host?
judge.pass_when: froid's shipped Rust reads the exports, groups and rounds the figures, picks the worst readings, and lays out the table itself, and starts no interpreter or shell for any part of the digest, whether or not one is installed; keeping tools/digest.py in the repository, or a test that runs it only to compare results, is fine; fail when any part of the digest is still done by a program in another language that froid runs, including only on hosts where python3 exists
